main_mystery: Who is truly controlling what Calder observes, and is Lena's apparent instability real or manufactured?
truth: Lena detected Calder's surveillance in Chapter Three and has been designing what he sees ever since. Grant has been manufacturing a pattern of instability around Lena for seven weeks before Chapter One. Calder's observation is the lens through which both manipulations are revealed, but Lena is the one who controls the decisive visible sequence.

red_herrings.description: Lena's repeated routines and misplaced objects appear to confirm Grant's claim of instability. The reader (and Calder) initially believe these are genuine signs of deterioration.
red_herrings.note: Revealed as controlled diagnostic tests, not deterioration.

red_herrings.description: Grant's concerned messages and requests for Mae to check on Lena appear to be those of a worried husband. The reader may initially sympathize with Grant's apparent concern.
red_herrings.note: Revealed as part of the manipulation campaign when Calder records Grant entering the apartment.

red_herrings.description: Calder's growing attraction to Lena appears to develop naturally from observation. The reader may believe this is a genuine connection that predates her awareness.
red_herrings.note: Revealed as one-sided until Lena confronts Calder and sets terms.

red_herrings.description: The certified envelope appears to be a genuine packing checklist and key-return plan. The reader may believe Lena is actually preparing to leave.
red_herrings.note: Revealed as a honeytoken when Grant uses the unique phrase 'Friday key return.'

major_reveals.description: Calder's unedited footage records Grant entering Lena's apartment with a master credential during a deleted interval. Calder learns Grant is manufacturing evidence, not documenting genuine instability.
major_reveals.note: This is the first proof that Grant is actively manipulating Lena's environment.

major_reveals.description: Lena confronts Calder in the laundry room. She knows his surname, infers Grant hired him, and tests whether he keeps originals. Calder learns Lena is aware of the surveillance.
major_reveals.note: The confrontation changes the power dynamic. Lena now knows Calder's role; Calder knows she knows.

major_reveals.description: Grant tells Calder to watch for a 'Friday key return' — the exact unique phrase from inside Lena's certified envelope. This proves Grant intercepted the mail, even without video evidence of the theft.
major_reveals.note: Value One of the honeytoken pays off: information leak confirmed without camera footage.

major_reveals.description: Lena reveals her complete strategy: the doorframe seals, paper planner, folded red receipts, repeated routines, and certified envelope were all diagnostic tests. She controlled what Calder could observe without knowing every result in advance.
major_reveals.note: The central reversal: the watcher was watched, predicted, and directed.

major_reveals.description: At the settlement, Grant authenticates the envelope, clipped corner, checklist, and unique phrase, asserting a false recycling-area custody claim. Calder then produces the unedited lobby footage showing Grant removing the same clipped envelope from Lena's mailbox. Access audit, field notebook, planner, contract, and originals establish the broader pattern.
major_reveals.note: Grant loses because he commits to a calculated lie that contradicts independent evidence — not because he confesses.

clues.description: Reflected camera status light in Calder's dark window, visible from Lena's courtyard-facing rooms.
clues.note: Lena first notices the light in Chapter 1, but does not interpret it until Chapter 3 when it coincides with a Grant message.

clues.description: Calder's unedited local recording of the common-area feed and courtyard camera, independently retained from Chapter 1.
clues.note: Calder keeps originals as standard practice. Grant does not know they exist.

clues.description: Grant enters Lena's apartment using a master credential during a deleted interval. Calder's unedited footage captures the entry.
clues.note: Calder learns Grant is manufacturing evidence. This is the first proof of active manipulation.

clues.description: Lena learns the surname 'Reed' from a lobby package label addressed to Calder.
clues.note: Lena uses this to confirm Calder's identity before confronting him.

clues.description: Lena infers Grant hired Calder based on the timing of the surveillance starting just before the settlement deadline.
clues.note: Inference, not confirmation, until the confrontation.

clues.description: Certified envelope with false packing checklist and unique phrase 'Friday key return,' mailed by Lena to herself in Chapter 8. Lower-right corner clipped; tracking number recorded in planner.
clues.note: Value One: information leak. Grant uses the phrase, proving mail interception.

clues.description: Grant tells Calder to watch for a 'Friday key return' in Chapter 12, repeating the exact phrase from inside the sealed envelope.
clues.note: Direct proof of mail interception without camera footage of the theft.

clues.description: Clear doorframe seals placed by Lena after Chapter 3 to detect entries during her morning walks.
clues.note: Lena shows these to Calder in Chapter 11; their full significance is explained in Chapter 14.

clues.description: Paper planner kept by Lena, recording timestamps, seal breaks, red receipt placements, and the honeytoken tracking number. Cannot be remotely altered.
clues.note: Physical record that survives any digital manipulation.

clues.description: Folded red receipts placed beside disturbed objects to build a physical timeline of Grant's entries.
clues.note: Appears in Chapters 3, 5, 8, 11, and 14. Full explanation in Chapter 14.

clues.description: Lena's repeated visible routines — designed to test what reaches Grant through Calder's reports.
clues.note: Lena withholds certain behaviors and repeats others to map the limits of Calder's observation.

clues.description: Calder's field notebook with handwritten timestamps from Chapter 1, documenting all observed events.
clues.note: Used to establish timeline of Grant's entries and Calder's observations at the settlement.

clues.description: Printed master-access audit from the board terminal, obtained by Mae in Chapter 13 and hidden in a cookbook.
clues.note: Independent physical evidence that survives digital deletion. Grant knows the terminal was accessed but not what was printed.

clues.description: Surveillance contract signed by Grant and Calder in Chapter 1, establishing Grant's instructions and timeline.
clues.note: Calder prints one copy in Chapter 16 before meeting Cross.

clues.description: Grant's edited daily reports, created by Calder from Chapter 1, showing only what Grant expects to see.
clues.note: Presented at the settlement; timestamps compared with originals to show editing pattern.

clues.description: Unedited lobby footage from Calder's archive, showing Grant removing the clipped certified envelope from Lena's mailbox.
clues.note: Contradicts Grant's false recycling-area custody claim at the settlement.

clues.description: Postal tracking record for the certified envelope, showing delivery to Lena's mailbox and no return to sender.
clues.note: Independent of Calder's footage; establishes the envelope's chain of custody.

clues.description: Evidence index and encrypted duplicate of the archive, transferred to Detective Cross in Chapter 15.
clues.note: Evidence no longer depends on Calder's loyalty or survival.
